tickets.title: Improvement: GitHub Sync Health Dashboard with Persistent Error Tracking
tickets.description:
### Problem

The background GitHub poller is completely opaque to users:
- When a sync fails (401 bad token, 404 repo deleted, rate limit, network timeout), the only evidence is a server log line — `log.exception("GitHub poll failed for link_id=%s", lid)`.
- The `GithubLink` model has `last_synced_at` but **zero error-tracking columns** (`last_error`, `last_error_at`, `error_count`).
- The UI shows `last_synced_at` as a date or `—`, with no error indicator. A link that has been failing for days looks identical to one that never synced.
- There is **no manual "Sync now" button** in the GitHub tab — users must go to Settings > CommitReadinessCard and click "Fix" (which calls the sync API), or use the raw API directly.
- Readiness checks only verify `last_synced_at IS NOT NULL` — they don't check if the last sync failed.

### Design

**Backend (3 changes):**

1. **Add error-tracking columns to `GithubLink` model and DDL:**
   - `last_error TEXT` — human-readable error message from the last failed sync
   - `last_error_at TIMESTAMPTZ` — when the last failure occurred
   - `error_count INT DEFAULT 0` — consecutive failure count
   - `sync_status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'idle'` — `idle` | `syncing` | `error` | `disabled` (so the UI can always show current status without hitting the GitHub API)

2. **Update `github_background.py` catch block** to persist error state to the DB on failure instead of just logging and rolling back silently.

3. **Add `GET /v1/projects/{id}/github/sync-status` endpoint** that returns per-link sync health (status, last_synced_at, last_error, last_error_at, error_count) — a lightweight read endpoint the UI can poll without triggering a sync.

**Frontend (3 changes):**

4. **GitHub tab** (`/projects/[id]/github/page.tsx`): Add a "Sync now" button next to each linked repo that calls `POST /sync`. Show sync status per repo as a colored badge (green/idle, yellow/syncing, red/error with the error message on hover).

5. **GitHub Settings** (`GitHubSettingsForm.tsx`): Replace the bare `last_synced_at` column with a sync status badge + relative time. Show `last_error` inline for errored links.

6. **DateDisplay** — actually use the existing `DateDisplay` component for timestamps so users see "2m ago" instead of absolute UTC dates (the original TPR-T-5 fix).

### Why this solves the user's real pain

When the user asks "why are commits not being pulled" or "is this an error?", the system currently has no answer beyond server logs. With this dashboard:
- The user sees instantly that a link is in `error` status with "401 — token expired"
- They can click "Sync now" to retry without leaving the page
- The error count shows whether the problem is transient or persistent
- In production, ops can check sync health at a glance rather than grepping logs

### Effort estimate

| Component | Files to change | Complexity |
|-----------|----------------|------------|

tickets.title: "Sync now" button on the GitHub tab
tickets.description:
Problem: When commits aren't showing, the user's only recourse is navigating to Settings → Commit Readiness → click "Fix" (which triggers a sync). The GitHub tab itself — where the user sees missing commits — has no sync control.
Change: Add a "Sync now" button per linked repo on the GitHub tab page (/projects/[id]/github/page.tsx), calling POST /v1/projects/{id}/github/links/{link_id}/sync. Show a spinner while syncing and a brief success/error toast.
Why small & impactful:
- ~20 lines added to a single file (page.tsx)
- No backend changes needed (the sync endpoint already exists)
- Gives users immediate control: they see missing commits → click "Sync now" → commits appear
- Solves the trust problem: the user can verify the pipe works right from the page that shows the data
Tradeoff: No persistent error tracking (that's the medium/large proposal). This is just a trigger button — it doesn't tell you why a previous sync failed.
